title: The Four Ways to Represent a Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the four standard ways to represent a function and give a quick example situation for each.
finalAnswer: Verbally (a sentence or formula describing the rule), numerically (a table of input-output pairs), visually (a graph), and algebraically (an explicit formula such as $f(x) = 2x + 1$).

steps.title: Verbal and Algebraic Description
steps.mathExpression: f(x) = \text{(area of a square with side } x\text{)} = x^2
steps.explanation: A function can be stated in words, such as the area of a square is the side length squared, and in a pure mathematical language, the formula f(x) = x^2. The verbal form carries meaning; the algebraic form carries precision.
steps.why: Formulas allow exact computation, while verbal statements make the modeling intent clear.

steps.title: Numerical Representation
steps.explanation: A table lists selected inputs alongside their outputs. Tabular representation is unavoidable when data come from measurement, such as temperature readings recorded every hour, and shows exact values even when no formula is known.
steps.why: Tables are the natural representation for discrete, measured, or tabulated real data.

steps.title: Visual Representation and Translation Between Forms
steps.explanation: The graph plots every point (x, f(x)) and reveals trends, symmetry, maxima, and intercepts at a glance. A skilled student moves fluently among all four forms: from formula to table, from table to graph, from graph back to a verbal story.
steps.why: Review questions test conceptual mastery, which is exactly the ability to translate between representations.
